definitions.explanation: A retail shop or store, typically a smaller independent establishment. Often used in compound forms, especially in {商店街|しょうてんがい} (shopping street/district).

examples.japanese: {駅前|えきまえ}に{小|ちい}さな{商店|しょうてん}がある。
examples.english: There is a small shop in front of the station.

examples.japanese: {商店街|しょうてんがい}を{歩|ある}いて{買|か}い{物|もの}をした。
examples.english: I walked through the shopping street and did some shopping.

examples.japanese: {地方|ちほう}の{商店街|しょうてんがい}はシャッター{通|どお}りと{呼|よ}ばれるほど{閉店|へいてん}が{相次|あいつ}いでいる。
examples.english: Shopping streets in rural areas have seen so many closures that they are called 'shutter streets.'

notes:
Most commonly encountered in the compound {商店街|しょうてんがい} (shopping street, shopping district) — a traditional row of small shops along a street, often covered with an arcade. These are a distinctive feature of Japanese neighborhoods.

As standalone {商店|しょうてん}, it sounds somewhat formal. In everyday speech, {店|みせ} or お{店|みせ} is more common for 'shop.'

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{商店街|しょうてんがい} — shopping street, shopping district
・{商店|しょうてん}{主|しゅ} — shopkeeper
・{個人|こじん}{商店|しょうてん} — independently owned shop
・{商店|しょうてん}が{並|なら}ぶ — shops line up (along a street)
